contract.agent: Existing book/global list_host_commands and execute_host_command consume the same service on demand, not a perpetual observation loop.

observations.result: No-grant worker observed no catalog. Read-only initial state had 18 disabled descriptors with no checked values. Fully granted initial state included authorized checked values and enabled actions, revision 1.

Agent-origin shelf.layout=list commit changed full worker layout-list from checked=false/revision1 to true/revision2; read-only worker remained at its single initial delivery because its hidden setting projection did not change.

Library Desk 0.6 Workspace > Host commands retained the typed search 'list view' while a committed settings change added Selected to Switch to list view. A remote-tagged KV write followed by flush changed layout back to grid; Selected disappeared without clearing search or replacing the dialog.

Library-write-only worker initially observed go-stats enabled. Opening the owned synthetic FB2 changed its next observation to disabled with reader-control. Existing book Agent go-shelf closed the reader through shared execution.

Changing host language from en to zh-Hans changed the read worker's title from Library to 书库 on the next delivery; language restored. Full worker host-unwatch returned 3 and a subsequent committed sort change left its stored delivery count at 3.

Targeted SQLite BEFORE UPDATE refusal for read-aware-shelf-view left grid unchanged and native search open at revision6. Exactly one role=status contained the localized database failure, without raw SQL. Removing the trigger and retrying list-view closed search at revision7.

After the previous toast expired, a legacy localKV.setItem on the same faulted shelf key rolled back to grid and displayed exactly one global Change not saved notice. Caller-owned domain failure did not suppress unrelated store-owned operations.

A new targeted SQL refusal made the compiled plugin grid-view click show exactly one localized status notice while preserving the command dialog and 'grid view' search. Removing the trigger and clicking again saved grid and closed the dialog.

unitEvidence: Observer stale reads are discarded, slow handlers coalesce, unchanged projections deduplicate, stable read errors recover, disposed reads are aborted and late delivery suppressed.
64 subscriptions are bounded, failed registrations release capacity, handler exceptions are logged and later changes still deliver.

Plugin read failure retains prior rows, displays stable inline error and removes actions; recovery restores actions. Each callback keeps its own snapshot revision, and retirement suppresses publication.

Settings rollback precedes caller-owned failure event; legacy default event still presents globally. Mixed queued operations retain independent failure ownership rather than using a global suppression flag.
captureBoundary: The 1200x800 capture shows the live filtered command and Selected check. The 800x650 later capture shows the preserved native command frame but not the earlier transient toast; notice counts are supported by contemporaneous DOM observations, not that screenshot. No document horizontal overflow at 800.

validation.build: Frontend production build and explicit Library Desk build passed

documents.drawerAndTheme: Matrix/model mobile drawer sets and clears main.inert; theme survives reload. Plugin-system has neither control.
documents.audit: No document horizontal overflow, duplicate IDs, broken fragment anchors, unnamed buttons or browser errors; observed CDN responses 200. No new diagrams.
documents.boundary: Static documentation checks are not product runtime evidence.

boundaries: Observation revision is per subscription, not a cross-actor clock, workspace revision, settings CAS or execution reservation.
Only settings-domain batches opt into caller presentation. Other async store facades are not declared migrated; legacy defaults remain store-owned.
Read failure/recovery, delayed-read and callback concurrency limits were unit-tested, not all injected into Tauri. Remote-tagged local writes are not a real cross-device sync campaign.
UI03 stays partial: target-specific availability, import tasks, cross-plugin invocation, remaining native entrypoints and complete focus remain open.
No packaged build, Windows/Linux, full install/upgrade consent or autonomous model inference was verified in this unit. Existing native/bridge/chunk warnings remain.
